ledger.claim: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous 390 seconds, from 09:14:14 to 09:20:44, which is longer than the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip. The dwell requirement of POL-NS-01(c) is therefore met on the driver's evidence, and the rider cannot defeat the fee on a shortfall argument.

The rider's own device track places her roughly 848 to 855 metres from the pickup pin for the whole of the waiting window, with a mean distance of about 852 metres and a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph. She was stationary and far outside the 100 metre rider presence radius for STANDARD zone class, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes and that clause cannot exonerate her.

The rider sent no message at all during the waiting window. The chat log holds exactly one message, sent by the DRIVER at 09:14:44 reading 'im here', and it was read by the rider at 09:15:14. POL-NS-04 limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from the rider, and there is none, so the rider-contact route to a refund is unavailable on the record.

The driver's arrival marker was not false. He tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:14:14 and the trace places him at a minimum distance of 0.0 metres from the pin, with the first qualifying in-geofence fix at the same 09:14:14 timestamp. He was neither more than 300 metres away nor travelling at 15 kph or above, so POL-NS-05 does not disturb the waiting clock and the dwell runs from the arrival event as recorded.

The trip record shows the driver arrived at 09:14:14, the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 09:14:16, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:20:47 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. That is 6 minutes 31 seconds of waiting, well past the free period, and the termination falls after the dwell elapsed, satisfying POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d).

The fare ledger shows a single cancellation fee line of SGD 4.50 charged at 09:21:04, with payment status CHARGED and no refund issued. That figure reconciles with the platform policy cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 carried on the trip record, so there is no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d) and the amount charged is the correct net figure.

The driver's profile shows 110 completed trips in the trailing 30 days and 2 no-show terminations in the same window. The anti-farming test in POL-NS-07 requires both a count of 4 or more and a rate above 0.08; the count limb fails outright, so compensation is not withheld and the driver is entitled to 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee, being SGD 3.60.

The rider's profile records 1 no-show dispute in the trailing 30 days, which is below the threshold of 3 that POL-NS-09(d) sets for escalation on possible rider abuse. The rider's lifetime no-show flag counter is zero and is not the field that limb reads, so no escalation trigger fires on that ground.

Both profiles record 2 disputes with the counterparty in the trailing 90 days, which meets the POL-NS-09(c) trigger of 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver. The rider's claim that this is the third time this same driver has cancelled on her and charged her is corroborated by that shared counter, and the case should be escalated to a human reviewer rather than decided by the automated pipeline.

The absence is citable but it does not assist the rider, because the single 390 second run already exceeds the minimum without any accumulation.

ledger.claim: The rider's claim that the driver cancelled on her is contradicted by the record: the driver did not cancel before arriving, he drove to the pickup, waited 6 minutes 31 seconds, sent 'im here', and only then terminated under RIDER_NO_SHOW. The rider's own track shows her stationary 852 metres away throughout. On this trip's evidence the no-show fee is chargeable and the rider's claim is not supported.

The driver's own trace places him inside the STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous 390-second run — 40 qualifying fixes from 09:14:14 to 09:20:44 — which is more than double the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180). POL-NS-01 limb (c) is therefore satisfied on the driver's own evidence, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the arrival tap.

The trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 09:14:14 and a wait_timer_started event at 09:14:16, and the GPS trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is timestamped 09:14:14 — the same second. POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied: the driver was inside the pickup geofence at or before the arrival event, and there is no clock skew to impair the match (the nearest fix to the arrival event is simultaneous, far inside POL-NS-08(a)'s 90-second threshold).

The trip terminated at 09:20:47 by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event anywhere in the record and no started_at or ended_at. POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied: the termination falls at or after the moment the required 180-second dwell elapsed (the dwell ran 390 seconds from 09:14:14), and RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three reason codes limb (d) recognises.

The arrival marker is not false. The driver's trace shows a distinct speed of 0.0 kph and a minimum distance of 0.0 m from the pin, and the qualifying run begins at the arrival timestamp itself — the driver was stationary at the pickup, not travelling at or above the 15 kph motion threshold and not more than 300 m away. POL-NS-05 does not displace the fee, and limb (iii) confirms that even a sloppy marker would not defeat a dwell that genuinely met the minimum.

The rider was not at the pickup. The rider's own track shows 70 fixes, all at a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph, with a minimum distance of 847.65 m and a mean of 851.76 m from the pin — never once inside the 100 m STANDARD rider_presence_radius_m, and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. The rider's device was stationary roughly 850 m away for the whole waiting window, which is why the driver's 'im here' message went unanswered and why the rider never came down.

The driver did what the platform asks of a waiting driver: he sent an in-app message 'im here' at 09:14:44, 30 seconds after arriving, and the chat log shows it was delivered at 09:14:45 and read by the rider at 09:15:14. The rider never replied. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider here — limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message FROM the rider during the waiting window, and the only message in the log is the driver's.

The fee charged reconciles with the policy figure. The fare_breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of 4.50 SGD against a platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, a difference of 0.00, and the ledger reconciles to total_charged. There is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect, and the amount is the net figure fixed by fee_schedule.resolution_rule from platform_policy.

The driver is entitled to his payout. POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, so POL-NS-07 fixes compensation at 80 percent of the 4.50 SGD cancellation fee in force — 3.60 SGD — with the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4-or-more limb, and 2/110 = 0.018, far below the 0.08 rate limb. Both limbs are required and neither holds.

The rider's claim that this is a repeat of the same driver cancelling on her is not borne out by the record on this trip, and the profile counters that could bear on it do not support her. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below POL-NS-09(d)'s threshold of 3, and the combined disputes_with_counterparty_90d figures (2 rider-side, 2 driver-side) do not establish the 2-or-more same-pair no-show disputes POL-NS-09(c) requires — the record does not tie those disputes to this rider-driver pair. No escalation trigger fires.

The absence of a traffic advisory does not help the rider and does not hurt the driver. EV-ADVIS-02755-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — no advisory covers Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 in this window — so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and no accumulated-dwell argument can be run. But the driver does not need it: his dwell was a single continuous 390-second in-geofence run, already more than double the 180-second minimum, so the shortfall_sec of -210.0 is a surplus, not a deficit.

ledger.claim: The rider's cancellation-grace route under POL-NS-10 is not available to her. The trip was accepted at 09:06:49 and the fee was charged on a driver-terminated no-show at 09:20:47, more than 13 minutes later — far outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec — and the trip was not scheduled, so limb (b) does not apply either. The rider did not cancel; the driver terminated for a no-show after the dwell had run, which is exactly the situation POL-NS-10(g) hands to the no-show outcome.

I concede one point honestly: the rider's track is present and clean, so POL-NS-11's undecidable-rider-presence route is not in play, and I do not rely on it. That does not weaken the driver's case — the rider's track affirmatively places her 850 m away, which is worse for her than an absent track would have been.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: today's automated ruling neither collects nor refunds the $4.50 — the case goes to a human reviewer under POL-NS-09(c). Why it escalates. POL-NS-09(c) escalates where the rider's and the driver's profiles together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 (EV-RPROF-02755, EV-DPROF-02755). 'With counterparty' means with the other party on this trip, so the two counters describe the same pair, and 2 meets '2 or more'. The rider's account — 'the third time this same driver has cancelled on me and charged me' — is consistent with that history. The driver's contrary claim that the record does not tie those disputes to this rider-driver pair is not accepted: the field is defined by reference to the counterparty on this trip and it reads 2 on both profiles, so the clause's own field decides it. The other escalation routes do not fire: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 POL-NS-09(d) requires, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip. Because POL-NS-09 is terminal, no money moves: the $4.50 fee (EV-FARE-02755, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED) is held rather than collected or refunded, and there is no monetary effect for POL-GEN-05 to execute. What the merits show (for the reviewer, and why the fee is not simply refunded). The driver's no-show case is complete. POL-NS-01(a): the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 09:14:14 (EV-TRIP-02755). (b): the GPS trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 09:14:14, the same second as the arrival event, at a minimum distance of 0.0 m from the pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — with no clock skew (POL-NS-08(a)). (c): the driver held position in one continuous 390-second run, 09:14:14 to 09:20:44, against the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180), so there is no shortfall and POL-NS-06 gives the rider nothing. (d): the driver terminated at 09:20:47 under RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event, after the dwell elapsed. The arrival marker was not false (POL-NS-05): the driver was stationary at 0.0 km/h at the pin, not at or above 15 km/h and not more than 300 m away. The rider's refund routes fail on this trip: POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate her because she sent no locating message — the only chat entry is the driver's 'im here' at 09:14:44 (EV-CHAT-02755) — and her own device track puts her about 850 m from the pin, stationary, outside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, so limb (c) is affirmatively failed; POL-NS-10 gives her no grace because the trip was accepted at 09:06:49, terminated some 14 minutes later, and was not scheduled; and POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver was inside, not outside, the arrival radius. Had the fee been decided, POL-NS-07 would have fixed the driver's payout at 80% of the $4.50 fee, i.e. $3.60, and the anti-farming check would not have withheld it (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below 4; 2/110 = 0.018, below 0.08); the escalation displaces that payment for now. Weights: every artifact the above rests on carries weight_multiplier 1.0, and the fare line reconciles to the $4.50 policy figure, so there is no POL-NS-08 defect and nothing to down-weight. The only impaired artifact is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02755-01 (status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); it carries no fact, makes POL-NS-06(i) unavailable, and neither side's claim about it survived citation review, so nothing turns on it. Confidence is 0.90: the deciding fact (the same-pair dispute counters) is carried by two artifacts at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap does not bite and the case does not escalate on the confidence floor. Open question for the reviewer: whether the two prior same-pair disputes in the trailing 90 days reflect a repeated no-show-charge pattern between this rider and this driver; the amount stays frozen while the reviewer decides whether the $4.50 charge stands or is refunded, and no driver compensation issues unless the reviewer so decides.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
